clue.text: Detective sergeant pursues workman, to arrest him thus?

indicators.note: pursues means comes after, so the sergeant's name follows the workman

parts.note: a hand is a manual worker, as in a farm hand
Sergeant Cuff is the detective in Wilkie Collins's novel The Moonstone

explanation.surface: A detective sergeant chases a labourer, ready to clap the irons on him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Detective sergeant' looks like the DS abbreviation, but it names Sergeant Cuff of The Moonstone, the famous early fictional detective.
explanation.definitionFit: To shackle a suspect's wrists with metal bracelets is the usual way police secure someone being taken into custody.

clue.text: A place for medals, side by side

parts.note: medals are pinned on the left breast of a uniform

explanation.surface: Where medals are worn, shoulder to shoulder on parade.
explanation.definitionFit: In line, level with each other, as soldiers marching in a row.

clue.text: Folding tents and stealing away?

explanation.definitionFit: Literally breaking up a camp, and figuratively slipping off without notice.

clue.text: Like Pooh, insure for damage

indicators.note: damage means to break up, so the letters of the word insure are rearranged

explanation.surface: Cover for damage to a teddy bear, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for damage' signals an anagram of INSURE; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective for bears, and Winnie-the-Pooh is a bear.

clue.text: He was stigmatized as a man of no property

definitions.text: He was stigmatized as a man of no property

parts.words: He was stigmatized as a man of no property
parts.note: stigmatized means bearing the wounds of Christ, not disgraced; this friar received them and vowed poverty

explanation.definitionFit: The thirteenth-century founder of the Franciscans renounced wealth and is said to have received the stigmata.

clue.text: Mixed materials won by students' charity do

indicators.note: by here means beside, so the two pieces stand next to each other

parts.note: rag is the annual fundraising event run by British university students
to bag something is to win or secure it

explanation.surface: Some odds and ends of cloth have been raised at a student fundraiser.
explanation.walkthrough: RAG week is a British student tradition of stunts and collections for charity.
explanation.definitionFit: A miscellaneous collection, originally a bag for scraps of cloth, hence any jumble of assorted stuff.

clue.text: German-American writer sound comment?

indicators.note: sound here means as heard, so the word comment is replaced by one pronounced the same

parts.note: a remark is a comment

explanation.surface: A writer from Germany who settled in America makes a sound observation.
explanation.walkthrough: Erich Maria Remarque wrote All Quiet on the Western Front and later took US citizenship. 'sound' looks like an adjective (sensible) but signals the homophone.
explanation.definitionFit: Erich Maria Remarque, author of All Quiet on the Western Front, was born in Germany and became a US citizen.

clue.text: Dibdin's tight little situation? Right

parts.note: Thomas Dibdin's patriotic song The Tight Little Island celebrated his homeland, a place well situated off Europe

explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Dibdin's song The Tight Little Island was a popular 19th-century patriotic number; 'situation' stands for the island it sang of.
explanation.definitionFit: Dibdin's song The Tight Little Island is about the island nation off northwest Europe.

clue.text: Wooster was one, and Jeeves was his

definitions.meaning: Bertie Wooster, of P. G. Wodehouse's stories, was a man of good birth and leisure
Jeeves was Wooster's valet, a ... ..., so Wooster's man

explanation.definitionFit: Bertie was a well-born man of leisure, and a valet is a gentleman's personal manservant, so Jeeves was his.

clue.text: Mugger gets us. What a bloomer!

parts.note: the mugger is the Indian marsh crocodile, so a croc

explanation.surface: Someone is robbed and the victim exclaims at what a blunder that was.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mugger' suggests a street robber, but it is the name of an Indian crocodile; 'bloomer' suggests a mistake, but here it is something that blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloomer is a plant that flowers, and this early spring corm is one.

clue.text: Old country-man member has Annie worried

parts.note: an arm is a limb, a member of the body

indicators.note: worried means pulled about and disturbed, so the name's letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An elderly countryman in some organisation upsets a woman called Annie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' rearranges ANNIE into ENIAN after ARM. 'Old country-man' reads as a rustic, but it means a man of an ancient country.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of the ancient Caucasian nation, one of the oldest Christian kingdoms.

clue.text: Musical tone a mouth-organ largely provides

indicators.note: largely means most of it, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a mouth-organ is the small reed instrument played by blowing, also called a harmonica

explanation.surface: A mouth-organ supplies most of a piece's musical notes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'largely' drops the last letter, A, from the instrument's name.
explanation.definitionFit: An overtone, a component frequency sounding above the fundamental of a note, is called by this name in acoustics.

clue.text: Remember to ring again

definitions.meaning: to telephone someone a second time

explanation.definitionFit: Bringing a memory back, or phoning back, both use the word: call back to mind or call back on the telephone.

clue.text: Lofty sort of wit?

parts.note: a room up in the loft, and also the refined, elegant humour associated with ancient Athens

explanation.definitionFit: The top-floor room under the roof shares its name with the classical Athenian style, as in that famous phrase about refined humour.

clue.text: Noah, cotton-spinning inventor?

definitions.meaning: Noah built the ark, and a wright is a builder, so Noah was an ark-builder
Richard ... invented the water frame for spinning cotton

explanation.definitionFit: Richard Arkwright patented the spinning frame, and split as a builder of the ark the name fits Noah.

clue.text: Bell was 25's (£25 including dues returned to Monsieur)

indicators.note: to here means added on, so the last piece comes at the end
including means holding something within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a pony is British slang for twenty-five pounds

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the word dues is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
M is the abbreviation for the French title Monsieur

explanation.surface: A note on what a certain Bell was, with a sum of money and some fees paid back to a Frenchman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns DUES into SEUD, which sits inside PONY. Currer Bell was the pen name under which the sister at 25 published Jane Eyre.
explanation.definitionFit: A name assumed by an author in place of their real one, as a woman novelist publishing under a male-sounding name did.

clue.text: Like Dame Partlet, nothing over sixpence, as our new edition shows

indicators.note: over means placed above, which in a down entry puts the zero first

parts.note: O, the figure zero, is nothing
six is VI in Roman numerals and pence is abbreviated P

indicators.note: a new edition reworks a text, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Dame Partlet, with nothing above a sixpence, features in a revised version of our book.
explanation.walkthrough: Dame Partlet is the hen in Chaucer's Nun's Priest's Tale. 'new edition' rearranges AS OUR into AROUS; a sixpence was an old British coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Hens lay eggs, and the zoological term describes egg-laying animals.

clue.text: Elsa was introducing the archbishop into fern arrangement

indicators.note: into means put inside, so the signature goes within the rearranged plant
an arrangement of flowers puts them in new order, so the letters of fern are reshuffled

parts.note: Ebor is the signature of the Archbishop of York

explanation.surface: Elsa was bringing a senior bishop into a display of ferns.
explanation.walkthrough: Elsa was the lioness of the book Born Free. 'arrangement' turns FERN into FREN, and EBOR goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Elsa, the lioness in Joy Adamson's Born Free, was free from birth, which the word means.

clue.text: Royal barge ? The secret of keeping on top

definitions.meaning: a monarch's boat, read as a vessel for a ruler

definitions.text: The secret of keeping on top
definitions.meaning: the art of ruling, the skill a sovereign needs to stay in power

explanation.definitionFit: Statecraft for a monarch is the skill of governing; split, the word is a sovereign's vessel.

clue.text: One cracks it at table? He's crackers!

definitions.meaning: the shell of a nut, which diners crack open after dinner

explanation.definitionFit: Read literally it is the hard shell of a nut; as slang it is a madman.

clue.text: Mrs Tod sees the archdeacon about nine

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the title goes round the numeral

parts.note: an archdeacon is styled the Venerable, abbreviated Ven
IX is nine in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A lady encounters a senior clergyman at around nine o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: Tod is an old word for a fox, so Mrs Tod is a female fox.
explanation.definitionFit: Tod is dialect for a fox, and the wife of a fox is the female of the species.

clue.text: Tax-gatherer a retired Thespian?

definitions.meaning: one who demands and collects payments

explanation.definitionFit: One who extorts or collects dues; split, a former stage performer.

clue.text: Two Boys — a simple book

parts.note: Herb is a boy's name, short for Herbert
Al is a boy's name, short for Albert

explanation.surface: Two lads appear in an easy reader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'simple' looks like 'easy', but simples are medicinal plants, so a simple book is a book of plants.
explanation.definitionFit: Simples are medicinal plants, and a book describing plants and their uses is so named.

clue.text: What to do after a blow-out, go to bed

definitions.text: What to do after a blow-out
definitions.meaning: after a puncture you fit a new tyre, read as re-tyre
to turn in for the night

explanation.definitionFit: To turn in for the night, and punningly to fit a fresh tyre after a puncture.

clue.text: Wrecked seaplane. What a life for Adullamites!

indicators.note: wrecked means smashed up, so the letters of the aircraft are rearranged

explanation.surface: A flying boat has crashed, and someone exclaims at the life led by some biblical exiles.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Bible David's followers hid in the cave of Adullam, so Adullamites lived like cave-dwellers.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means cave-dwelling, from the Greek for a cave, as David's band in the cave of Adullam were.

clue.text: Pleased I owe £1 for flowers?

parts.note: glad means pleased
an IOU says I owe you, so I owe alone is IO
the pound sign is L and the figure 1 looks like the letter I

explanation.surface: Someone is relieved to be only a pound in debt.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is written out as an IOU might be: GLAD, then I O(we), then L1 for one pound.
explanation.definitionFit: These tall sword-leaved plants with spikes of bright blooms are garden blossoms.

clue.text: Brave soul, Emily

parts.note: Emily the novelist wrote the poem beginning No coward soul is mine, a brave soul indeed

explanation.definitionFit: The surname of Emily, author of Wuthering Heights and the poem No coward soul is mine.

clue.text: Entrap cunningly

indicators.note: cunningly means in a crafty, twisted way, so the six letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Set a crafty snare for someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cunningly' rearranges ENTRAP, and the whole clue is also the meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: An old verb meaning to lure or ensnare by trickery.

clue.text: See us in the punishment frame, beheaded? All done by mirrors

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so these two letters go within the shortened word
beheaded means losing the head, so the first letter is cut off

parts.note: a pillory is the wooden frame in which offenders were locked for public shaming
taken as written

explanation.surface: Picture us locked headless in the stocks: it must be a conjuring trick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beheaded' cuts P from PILLORY, leaving ILLORY, and 'in' puts US inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A conjuror's trick done with mirrors is deceptive, not real.
